\documentclass[../main.tex]{subfiles}
\usepackage{longtalbe}

\begin{document}
\section{Venice: The Convoy System and Its Costs}

The Venetian state organised long-distance trade
into seasonal convoys, the mude,
and auctioned the right to load goods on state galleys.
The system lowered protection costs for individual merchants
while giving the Senate fine-grained control
over the flow of strategic goods.

Freight rates from the auction books
survive for most of the fifteenth century
and are summarised below for the principal routes.

\begin{longtable}{lrr}
\hline
Route & Mean rate (ducat/char.) & Sailings \\
\hline
\endhead
Venice--Alexandria & 12.4 & 41 \\
Venice--Beirut & 11.7 & 38 \\
Venice--Constantinople & 8.9 & 52 \\
Venice--Bruges & 15.2 & 17 \\
\hline
\caption{Mean freight rates on state galleys, 1420--1460.}
\end{longtable}

The premium on the Bruges route reflects both distance
and the insurance load of Atlantic waters in winter.

\end{document}
